descriptionChirho: The Qal active participle of ra'ah used substantively to denote a shepherd or herdsman, one who tends flocks or herds. Applied to literal shepherds in the patriarchal narratives (Gen 13:7-8 'herdsmen of Abram/Lot', Gen 26:20 'shepherds of Gerar', 1 Sam 21:8 'the shepherds'), and extended metaphorically to rulers and leaders: God as 'my shepherd' in Isa 44:28 (of Cyrus) and Zech 13:7, and possessive 'my shepherd' (arb ra'in, kor 'naui mokja', spa 'mi pastor'). Consistently rendered across languages: arb ru'at (pl.), deu 'Hirten', fra 'bergers', hin 'charvahe', kor 'mokjadeul', spa 'pastores'. The construct forms (ro'ey, ro'i) and suffixed forms (ro'ay 'my herdsmen', ro'ekha 'your herdsmen') are all inflectional variants of this single participial sense.
